PUSH_GUIDE.ANDROID_STEP_2: The app team adds the Android app in Project settings → General → Your apps and puts google-services.json in the app.
PUSH_GUIDE.ANDROID_STEP_3: Open the app on a phone, sign in, allow notifications, then press Send test.
PUSH_GUIDE.FAIL_APNS_MISSING_TEXT: No APNs key in Firebase. Do section 3, steps 1–4. Then send the test again.
PUSH_GUIDE.FAIL_APNS_REJECTED_TEXT: Key ID or Team ID is wrong, or the key was revoked in Apple. Check both IDs; if revoked, make a new key and upload it again.
PUSH_GUIDE.FAIL_HEADING: 5. iOS test failed — what to do
PUSH_GUIDE.FAIL_NOTHING_SHOWS_TEXT: On the iPhone: Settings → Notifications → the app → Allow Notifications on. Turn off Focus / Do Not Disturb. If the app is open on screen, iOS shows the banner only if the app handles it.
PUSH_GUIDE.FAIL_NO_DEVICE_TEXT: Open the app on the iPhone, sign in, and tap Allow on the notification prompt.
PUSH_GUIDE.FAIL_STILL_TEXT: Send a test to an Android device. If Android works, the problem is iOS setup (section 3). If both fail, check the service account key (section 1).
PUSH_GUIDE.FAIL_TOKEN_EXPIRED_TEXT: The app was removed or reinstalled. Open the app again and sign in; it registers a new token. Blocks removes the old one.
PUSH_GUIDE.FAIL_WRONG_APP_TEXT: The iOS app in Firebase has a different Bundle ID than the installed app. Fix the Bundle ID in Firebase, or add the right iOS app.
PUSH_GUIDE.INTRO: All steps are in the Firebase console (console.firebase.google.com) unless marked Apple.
PUSH_GUIDE.IOS_HEADING: 3. iOS — APNs key (done in Apple and Firebase, not here)
PUSH_GUIDE.IOS_STEP_1: Apple: developer.apple.com → Certificates, IDs & Profiles → Keys → +.
PUSH_GUIDE.IOS_STEP_2: Tick Apple Push Notifications service (APNs) → Continue → Register → Download the .p8 file. It can be downloaded only once.
PUSH_GUIDE.IOS_STEP_3: Note the Key ID (on the key page) and the Team ID (top right, under your name).
PUSH_GUIDE.IOS_STEP_4: Firebase: Project settings → Cloud Messaging → Apple app configuration → APNs Authentication Key → Upload. Add the .p8, Key ID and Team ID.
PUSH_GUIDE.IOS_STEP_5: The iOS app in Firebase must have the same Bundle ID as the real app.
PUSH_GUIDE.IOS_STEP_6: The app team turns on Push Notifications in Xcode → Signing & Capabilities.
PUSH_GUIDE.KEY_STEP_1: Open your project in the Firebase console.
PUSH_GUIDE.KEY_STEP_2: Click the gear icon → Project settings → tab Service accounts.
PUSH_GUIDE.KEY_STEP_3: Click Generate new private key → Generate key. A .json file downloads.
PUSH_GUIDE.KEY_STEP_4: Upload this file here. Or use Enter manually: copy client_email and private_key from the file.
PUSH_GUIDE.KEY_STEP_5: Delete the downloaded file from your computer after saving.
PUSH_GUIDE.KEY_STEP_6: Check also: Project settings → Cloud Messaging must show "Firebase Cloud Messaging API (V1) — Enabled".
PUSH_GUIDE.TITLE: Setup guide — Push
PUSH_GUIDE.WEB_STEP_1: Project settings → General → Your apps. No web app yet? Click the </> icon and register one.
PUSH_GUIDE.WEB_STEP_2: Under SDK setup and configuration choose Config. Copy the whole firebaseConfig block and paste it here.
PUSH_GUIDE.WEB_STEP_3: VAPID key: Project settings → Cloud Messaging → Web Push certificates → Generate key pair. Copy the Key pair value.
PUSH_GUIDE.WEB_STEP_4: Manual entry: API key = apiKey, App ID = appId, Sender ID = messagingSenderId.
